title: CI matrix across operating systems and runtime versions
when: A library or command line tool must work on linux, windows and mac and on several runtime versions, and the user wants CI to prove it on each push.
prompt:
Goal: A matrix job that runs one suite on every supported OS and runtime version and names each failing combination.
Steps:
1. strategy.matrix.os lists the host's linux, windows and mac runner labels; matrix.node lists the majors from engines (20, 22, 24), or matrix.python 3.10 to 3.13 from requires-python.
2. strategy.fail-fast: false so one broken cell does not cancel the rest.
3. include adds one extra cell (newest runtime with an experimental flag); exclude drops unsupported pairs, each with a comment.
4. The job name shows the OS and version of the cell.
5. defaults.run.shell: bash so scripts behave alike everywhere.
6. .gitattributes with * text=auto eol=lf keeps LF endings on every checkout.
7. Lint, coverage and packaging run once in a separate job with needs: test.
8. Keep the version list, the engines field and the README table identical.
Quality bar:
- Every cell runs the same command.
- A failure title names OS and version.
- The matrix stays under about 12 cells.
Pitfalls:
- Tests that hardcode / separators or \n endings and fail on one OS.
- Runtime labels like latest, so the matrix changes without a commit.
- One copied job per OS instead of a matrix.
Verify:
- [ ] fail-fast is false.
- [ ] Versions match engines or requires-python.
- [ ] Actions are pinned.
- [ ] .gitattributes sets line endings.
Output: the CI workflow file matrix.yml, .gitattributes and a supported versions table in README.md.

examples.input: test my library on node 20, 22 and 24 on all three operating systems
examples.output: matrix.os with three runner labels, matrix.node [20, 22, 24], fail-fast false, shell bash, .gitattributes eol=lf
